title: Verify only partially completed preference questionnaire is accepted, with answered and unanswered fields tracked
description: This test verifies that the platform properly handles partial questionnaire submissions, tracking both answered and omitted fields for the seeker profile. It validates flexibility in onboarding and ensures that only explicit answers are used in matching. Automation: HIGH – API/ui assertions.
testDescription: A new seeker fills out only some of the preference questionnaire fields (e.g., working arrangement and motivator) while leaving others blank (e.g., salary, job titles, education). Upon submission, the platform accepts the incomplete form and records which preferences were provided and which were left unanswered.
prerequisites: Platform is available and questionnaire is presented to seeker without account; no previous preferences recorded.
stepsToPerform: 1. Load platform home page in new incognito session. 2. Start questionnaire flow. 3. Select 'Hybrid' for working arrangement. 4. Choose 'Flexibility' as motivator. 5. Leave 'annual salary', 'job titles', 'category', 'years experience', 'education', and 'workplace benefit' fields blank. 6. Submit questionnaire. 7. Observe partial completion notification (if any). 8. Confirm submission. 9. View recorded preferences in profile or confirmation modal.
expectedResult: Platform stores which fields were answered and which were left unanswered; personalized results reflect only provided preferences.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Record which preferences were provided and which were left unanswered.

title: Verify seeker can revisit and change any individual preference without repeating whole questionnaire
description: This test ensures that a seeker can update or modify any individual preference after the initial questionnaire submission without having to re-complete all fields. This upholds a business-critical UX improvement, allowing flexible adaptation of preferences. Automation: MEDIUM – UI assertion required.
testDescription: After completing the initial questionnaire, a seeker revisits their preference settings from the profile area and changes a single field (e.g., updates job titles from 'Software Engineer' to 'Data Analyst'), confirming that only the targeted preference is adjusted and the rest remain unchanged.
prerequisites: Seeker preferences previously completed and stored; seeker profile area is accessible on platform.
stepsToPerform: 1. Open platform as anonymous seeker; complete questionnaire with all fields. 2. Submit questionnaire. 3. Navigate to profile or preferences section. 4. Locate 'Job Titles' preference. 5. Select 'Edit' for job titles. 6. Remove 'Software Engineer' and add 'Data Analyst'. 7. Save updated preferences. 8. Confirm update is applied. 9. Check that other preferences remain unchanged. 10. Reload personalized listings to verify new preference effect.
expectedResult: Individual preference is changed successfully; other preferences are left intact; listings reflect updated preference.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Allow preferences to be revisited and changed later without the seeker having to repeat the whole questionnaire.

title: Verify job title list enforces maximum allowed number of selections and handles N-1/N/N+1 entries
description: This test verifies the boundary behavior of the job titles selection field, ensuring the platform only accepts up to the defined maximum, and properly handles exactly one below, at, and over limit cases. Prevents UI/input errors and helps seekers target relevant jobs. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: The seeker attempts to select: (a) N-1 job titles, (b) exactly N job titles, (c) N+1 job titles (where N is the defined max, e.g., 3). Platform accepts first two cases, rejects the third with a clear error. All cases are executed in sequence in a single session.
prerequisites: Defined maximum job titles is set in system config (e.g., N=3); questionnaire and job title field available.
stepsToPerform: 1. Start seeker onboarding questionnaire. 2. Select two job titles (N-1): 'QA Tester', 'DevOps Engineer'. 3. Attempt submission; confirm acceptance. 4. Edit job titles, select three (N): 'QA Tester', 'DevOps Engineer', 'Scrum Master'. 5. Submit; confirm acceptance. 6. Edit job titles, select four (N+1): 'QA Tester', 'DevOps Engineer', 'Scrum Master', 'Backend Developer'. 7. Submit; observe error message indicating maximum exceeded. 8. Verify only first N titles are stored.
expectedResult: Submission accepted with N-1 and N selections; error message shown and submission rejected for N+1; only valid job titles are stored.

sourceCitation.excerpt: the job titles the seeker is targeting, up to a defined maximum

title: Verify location field only accepts standard country/region values; rejects invalid or unlisted entries
description: This test ensures the location picker only accepts entries matching the standard list of countries or regions, and rejects invalid, misspelled, or unlisted values with error messaging. Supports data integrity and downstream matching accuracy. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: A seeker enters valid location ('Germany'), then invalid ('Atlantis'), malformed ('12345'), and misspelled ('Unite States'). The platform accepts only the valid location, rejects other types with error, and prevents submission if no valid value is present.
prerequisites: Standard country/region list is loaded in location field; platform questionnaire available.
stepsToPerform: 1. Open onboarding questionnaire. 2. Enter 'Germany' as location; proceed. 3. Edit location, enter 'Atlantis'; attempt submission. 4. Observe error message. 5. Enter '12345' as location; attempt submission. 6. Observe error message. 7. Enter 'Unite States' (misspelling); attempt submission. 8. Observe error message. 9. Enter 'United States' from list; confirm acceptance.
expectedResult: Valid country ('Germany', 'United States') accepted; invalid/unlisted/malformed values are rejected with error message and not stored.

sourceCitation.excerpt: the location the seeker will be working from, held against a standard list of countries and regions

title: Verify selection of working arrangement enforces options: fully remote, hybrid, or no preference
description: This test checks that the working arrangement field allows only the three stated values: fully remote, hybrid, or no preference. It covers all valid partitions, preventing invalid or custom values. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: Seeker completes the questionnaire by selecting each working arrangement option ('Fully Remote', 'Hybrid', 'No Preference'), and attempts an invalid entry ('Office-based'). Platform accepts only the valid three, rejects invalid with error feedback.
prerequisites: Platform is running; working arrangement field is available with three options; invalid string options blocked.
stepsToPerform: 1. Start seeker questionnaire. 2. Select 'Fully Remote'; submit; confirm acceptance. 3. Edit, select 'Hybrid'; submit; confirm acceptance. 4. Edit, select 'No Preference'; submit; confirm acceptance. 5. Edit, attempt to enter 'Office-based' (not selectable); submit. 6. Observe error message. 7. Ensure only valid options are stored.
expectedResult: Valid selections ('Fully Remote', 'Hybrid', 'No Preference') are accepted; invalid option is rejected with clear error.

sourceCitation.excerpt: the working arrangement sought (fully remote, hybrid, or no preference)

title: Verify seeker can declare current resume state as up to date, needs work, or not written yet
description: This test confirms that the seeker can indicate their resume status using the exact expected states, supporting accurate matching and guidance. Automation: HIGH – API/UI assertions.
testDescription: A seeker reaches the resume capture step and selects 'Up to date', then 'Needs work', and finally 'Not written yet', ensuring each status can be declared and is correctly stored under their profile. Resume guidance or upload prompts should reflect status.
prerequisites: Resume state options ('Up to date', 'Needs work', 'Not written yet') available in resume step; seeker has completed preference questionnaire.
stepsToPerform: 1. Complete preference questionnaire flow. 2. Navigate to resume step. 3. Select 'Up to date'; save; check status is stored. 4. Edit, select 'Needs work'; save; confirm update. 5. Edit, select 'Not written yet'; save; confirm update. 6. View profile; confirm current resume status. 7. Observe guidance/upload prompts reflecting chosen status. 8. End session; resume status persists.
expectedResult: Each resume state is selectable, stored, and reflected in seeker profile; prompts change based on state.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Capture the current state of the seeker's resume (up to date, needs work, not written yet).

title: Verify supported resume document formats are accepted and stored up to size limit
description: This test validates that only common document formats (e.g., PDF, DOCX) at or below the defined size limit are accepted and retained as part of the seeker profile. Ensures data integrity and compliance. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: Seeker uploads resumes in PDF (400KB) and DOCX (900KB) formats, both under the size limit (1MB), and confirms both are accepted and linked to their profile. Platform must display confirmation and use resumes for matching/applications.
prerequisites: Resume upload step available; supported formats and size limit (e.g., 1MB) specified; seeker is at resume step.
stepsToPerform: 1. Complete preference questionnaire. 2. Navigate to resume upload. 3. Select PDF (400KB) resume file 'test-seeker-001.pdf'; upload. 4. Observe confirmation of upload. 5. Select DOCX (900KB) resume file 'test-seeker-001.docx'; upload. 6. Observe confirmation. 7. View profile; resumes are stored. 8. Confirm resume is available for matching/applications.
expectedResult: Supported formats uploaded under size limit are accepted, confirmed, and stored against seeker profile for matching/application.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Accept a resume upload in the common document formats, up to a defined size limit.

title: Verify resume upload above size limit is rejected with a clear error message
description: This test ensures that resume files larger than the defined limit are rejected with a clear, source-grounded error reason, preventing data overflow and supporting user guidance. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: Seeker attempts to upload a PDF resume file ('test-seeker-001-large.pdf', 1.5MB) exceeding the 1MB limit. Platform rejects the upload, displays a clear error stating file size exceeded, and prevents resume storage.
prerequisites: Resume upload interface available; size limit set to 1MB; seeker is at resume step.
stepsToPerform: 1. Complete preference questionnaire. 2. Navigate to resume upload. 3. Select PDF resume file 'test-seeker-001-large.pdf' (1.5MB). 4. Attempt to upload file. 5. Observe file rejected and clear error message 'Document exceeds maximum size limit (1MB)'. 6. Confirm no resume stored in profile. 7. Retry upload with allowed file (400KB); confirm acceptance. 8. End session; confirm error state is not persisted.
expectedResult: Oversized resume file is rejected with clear, source-grounded error message; no file is stored unless within allowed limit.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Reject unsupported formats and oversized documents with a clear reason.

title: Verify resume upload in unsupported format is rejected with a clear error message
description: This test validates that any resume document uploaded in a format not listed as supported (e.g., TXT, RTF, PPTX) is rejected with a clear error, ensuring data integrity and preventing unusable profile records. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: A seeker attempts to upload resumes in unsupported formats: 'test-seeker-001.txt', 'test-seeker-001.rtf', 'test-seeker-001.pptx'. The platform rejects each file, displays a clear error specifying unsupported format, and prevents storage. Supported files remain accepted.
prerequisites: Resume upload step available; supported formats (PDF, DOCX) known; seeker is at resume step.
stepsToPerform: 1. Complete preference questionnaire flow. 2. Navigate to resume upload interface. 3. Select and upload 'test-seeker-001.txt'. 4. Observe rejection and error message 'Unsupported format'. 5. Select and upload 'test-seeker-001.rtf'. 6. Observe rejection and error. 7. Select and upload 'test-seeker-001.pptx'. 8. Observe rejection and error. 9. Upload 'test-seeker-001.pdf'. 10. Confirm acceptance of supported format.
expectedResult: All unsupported format resumes are rejected with clear error message; only files in allowed formats are accepted and stored.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Reject unsupported formats and oversized documents with a clear reason.

title: Verify uploaded resume is confirmed as received before it is associated with seeker's profile
description: This test ensures a seeker-uploaded resume is positively acknowledged as 'received' before it is persisted or displayed as part of the seeker's profile, protecting against incomplete uploads or system error. Automation: HIGH — UI/API validation.
testDescription: A job seeker, visiting the site for the first time without an account, uploads a resume document in a supported format and valid size as prompted during onboarding. The system must confirm the file's successful receipt prior to storing or displaying it as 'attached to profile'. The user must clearly see a confirmation message and the resume must not be shown in profile listings or used in matching/workflows unless that acknowledgment step has completed.
prerequisites: Backend resume upload endpoint reachable, home page available, supported document format and size value prepared, browser session in new/anonymous state.
stepsToPerform: 1. Open the job platform home page in a new browser session. 2. Begin the seeker onboarding flow by clicking 'Start Questionnaire'. 3. Advance through to the resume status question. 4. Select 'Resume is up to date' and opt to upload a resume. 5. Choose a valid resume file (e.g., 'test_resume.docx', 2MB). 6. Click 'Upload'. 7. Wait for system processing and observe for any upload progress/completion indicator. 8. Verify that an explicit confirmation (e.g., 'Resume received' message) is displayed to the user. 9. Navigate to the seeker's profile or any UI component showing attached resume status. 10. Confirm resume is shown as associated with profile only after the confirmation. 11. Attempt a page refresh or navigation; ensure association persists after confirmation. 12. Optionally, inspect backend state/logs to confirm no record is attached prior to displayed confirmation.
expectedResult: Resume is not treated as part of the seeker's profile or used in any workflow until a definitive 'resume received' confirmation is presented after upload completion; association only occurs after this confirmation.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Confirm that an uploaded document has been received before it is treated as part of the seeker's profile.

title: Verify personalised job listings are generated after preference capture
description: Verifies that, for a new or anonymous visitor, the platform generates and displays a set of job listings that are personalized based on submitted preferences. Ensures search value is delivered prior to forced registration/payment. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: A first-time visitor completes the onboarding questionnaire, submitting answers for working arrangement, motivator, location, job titles, and other relevant fields. No account exists. Upon completion, the site must display a results page where job listings are personalized — filtered and ranked based on the captured preferences. The listings set should directly reflect the preference criteria chosen by the user in the questionnaire.
prerequisites: Platform listings data exists, home page and onboarding UI accessible, browser session must not have existing account or login.
stepsToPerform: 1. Launch the job platform homepage. 2. Click 'Start Questionnaire' to begin onboarding. 3. Select 'Fully Remote' for working arrangement. 4. Pick 'Career Progression' as motivator. 5. Enter 'Canada' as current location. 6. Input 'Frontend Developer' as job title. 7. Complete remaining preference fields as prompted. 8. Submit all questionnaire answers. 9. Wait for onboarding process to complete and results page to load. 10. Observe the displayed job listings. 11. Check that listings are relevant to the provided preferences (e.g., remote Frontend Developer roles in Canada, prioritizing career progression). 12. Confirm no forced registration or payment is required to view these listings.
expectedResult: A personalized job listings set is shown, filtered and ranked using the seeker’s submitted preferences, and no registration/payment is enforced at this stage.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Produce a personalised set of listings once the seeker's preferences have been captured, filtered and ranked against those preferences.

title: Verify updating a preference triggers refreshed results applying updated filters
description: Validates that when a seeker changes any captured preference, the results page is re-filtered and re-ranked immediately to reflect the new criteria, improving discovery and avoiding stale matches. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: A visitor who has completed the onboarding questionnaire and is viewing personalized job results changes an individual preference (e.g., location or job title). Upon updating, the displayed listings must refresh to reflect only those roles that match the newly-entered value, not the previous one.
prerequisites: Anonymous session has completed the initial preference questionnaire and is on the personalised results page. Listings dataset available.
stepsToPerform: 1. Start the onboarding questionnaire as an anonymous user. 2. Fill out all preference fields, e.g., location: 'Germany', job title: 'Backend Engineer'. 3. Submit responses to display the personalized results page. 4. Observe the listings reflecting 'Backend Engineer' in 'Germany'. 5. Locate the UI to edit/change preferences. 6. Change location preference to 'Belgium'. 7. Save/submit the change. 8. Wait for listings page to update or reload. 9. Check that only jobs matching 'Backend Engineer' in 'Belgium' are now shown. 10. Repeat with changing job title or another filter, and verify similar re-filtering and re-ranking. 11. Optionally, reload page to check persistence across navigation in session.
expectedResult: Results shown are promptly refreshed and filtered based solely on the most recent preference update, overriding previous values.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Apply the captured preferences to subsequent searches for the remainder of the visit, and to later visits once an account exists.

title: Verify seeker can widen, narrow, or clear individual preferences from results
description: Checks that the seeker can adjust their job search by individually widening (e.g. more locations), narrowing (e.g. more criteria), or clearing (removing) any preference in the filter set, and observes instant effect in results. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: After initial onboarding, a seeker reviews their personalised results. The seeker uses the UI controls to clear the job title, add another location, or apply additional filters. The system must instantly show a broader, narrower, or different listings set in response to these filter changes, without requiring resubmission of the full questionnaire.
prerequisites: Personalised results are displayed after onboarding questionnaire; seeker is not registered.
stepsToPerform: 1. Complete the onboarding questionnaire as a new visitor. 2. Reach the personalised job results page with filtered set. 3. Click to expand the 'Location' filter. 4. Add a new country/region (e.g., add 'UK' to 'Canada'). 5. Confirm an increased results set appears with jobs from both countries. 6. Remove (clear) an individual preference, e.g., job title filter. 7. Confirm broader results appear (various jobs, not just the previously-selected title). 8. Apply a new category or benefit filter to narrow results. 9. Verify jobs shown match the narrowed criteria. 10. Optionally, repeat steps with other preference types to confirm effects.
expectedResult: Each filter action (widen, narrow, clear) dynamically and correctly updates the displayed listings set in line with the changed preference(s) only.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Allow the seeker to widen, narrow or clear any individual preference from the results.

title: Verify seeker is informed when few job listings are found and shown which constraint is narrowing results
description: Ensures when preference combinations are overly restrictive (e.g., few or zero results), the UI alerts the seeker and explicitly identifies the constraint or filter most responsible for this narrowing. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: A user answers the onboarding with highly-specific preferences, resulting in one or very few matching listings. The results UI must display a message indicating 'Few listings found' and highlight (e.g. ‘Your job title filter is very specific’) the precise field or filter responsible for the restricted result set, helping the seeker relax constraints.
prerequisites: Backend supports preference-driven filtering and UI displays constraint messages; job dataset has partitionable results.
stepsToPerform: 1. Begin onboarding as new visitor. 2. Enter highly specific preferences—e.g., job title: 'Obscure Niche Role', location: 'Vanuatu', salary: very high value, category: 'Quantum Cheese Analysis'. 3. Submit the questionnaire. 4. Wait for the results page. 5. Observe the number of listings presented (expect 1 or zero based on dataset). 6. Look for a visible warning or info message that few matches were found. 7. Confirm that the UI highlights or names the filter(s) responsible (e.g., 'job title' or 'location'). 8. Optionally, adjust a specific constraint and verify removal or update of the notice.
expectedResult: A conspicuous info message appears when results are few, and the filter(s) most limiting the set are identified by name for the user.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Where a combination of preferences returns very few listings, indicate which constraint is narrowing the set.

title: Verify registration is not required for browsing, completing questionnaire, or seeing matched results
description: Checks that a new or anonymous visitor is never forced to register or pay for browsing job listings, questionnaire completion, or viewing personalized results, ensuring a frictionless value-first journey. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: An unregistered user accesses the home page, completes the onboarding questionnaire, and views personalised job listings. At no point should the flow require account creation or payment info. The user is able to repeat these actions multiple times in the session.
prerequisites: No account or payment required flags enabled on backend; home page, onboarding, and results UIs online.
stepsToPerform: 1. Open job platform homepage in incognito/private mode. 2. Access job listings/search without logging in. 3. Start and complete onboarding questionnaire with various answers. 4. Submit responses. 5. Observe personalized results. 6. Click back to home or perform another search. 7. Repeat questionnaire with different preferences. 8. Verify at all points no login, registration, or payment gate appears. 9. Attempt to view another listing in detail. 10. Confirm continued access without registration.
expectedResult: Browsing, questionnaire completion, and matched results viewing all remain accessible to anonymous visitors, no forced sign-up or paywall is introduced at these stages.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Browsing listings, completing the questionnaire and viewing matched results require no account and no payment.

title: Verify registration is only requested when seeker applies, saves, or sets up alerts on a listing
description: Ensures registration is deferred until a seeker takes direct action on a listing — applying, saving, or subscribing for alerts. Prevents premature acquisition friction until real value is demonstrated. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: A visitor, having completed onboarding and viewing personalized listings, attempts to read, browse, and search, encountering no registration prompt. When the user tries to save a job, apply for it, or set up job alerts, the registration screen appears — and only then.
prerequisites: Backend supports event-driven registration gating, job listing actions enabled, no current login/account.
stepsToPerform: 1. Navigate to platform homepage as a non-logged-in visitor. 2. Complete onboarding questionnaire. 3. View personalized job results. 4. Click on several jobs to read their details. 5. Confirm no registration prompt appears. 6. Attempt to save a job listing. 7. Observe system behavior. 8. Verify registration/signup prompt is now shown. 9. Cancel out — return to job results. 10. Try to apply for a job; confirm registration dialog is shown again. 11. Attempt to set up job alerts, confirming registration gate each time.
expectedResult: Registration or signup prompt is shown only upon 'apply', 'save', or 'set up alerts' actions, and not for passive browsing or searching.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Registration is requested only when the seeker acts on a listing — applying, saving it, or setting up alerts.

title: Verify preferences and resume captured before registration persist in the account after signup
description: Validates that preferences and any uploaded resume added during an anonymous session are properly persisted and linked to the seeker’s account upon successful signup, so onboarding effort/value is not lost. Automation: MEDIUM.
testDescription: An anonymous seeker completes onboarding and uploads a resume, but does not register. Later, they trigger registration (by applying for a job). After creating an account, they log in, and all their previously captured preferences and resume remain associated and are visible, eliminating duplicate effort.
prerequisites: Supports pre-registration data capture, account creation and linking; backend state carries from session to account.
stepsToPerform: 1. Open the job platform as an anonymous visitor. 2. Complete the onboarding questionnaire. 3. Upload a valid resume file when prompted. 4. Submit to view personalized results. 5. Take an action requiring registration (e.g., attempt to apply to a job). 6. Complete registration/signup workflow using 'test+carryover@example.com'. 7. Log in with the new credentials. 8. Navigate to profile preferences and resume section. 9. Verify all previously entered preferences and the uploaded resume are present. 10. Optionally, perform another results search and confirm it matches initial preferences. 11. Repeat logout/login to confirm data association persists.
expectedResult: All preferences and uploaded resume from pre-signup session are visible and active in the new account after registration.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Preferences captured before registration carry over into the account when the seeker signs up.

title: Verify preferences and uploaded documents are held during anonymous session and under account after signup
description: Checks PII and resume file persistence both for sessions with no login (held throughout) and after account registration (carried over). Ensures onboarding value-chain integrity, with sensitive data lifespan aligned to user state. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: A visitor completes the onboarding questionnaire and uploads a valid resume file. They navigate away, return within the session (without logging out or closing browser), and confirm all inputs and upload remain intact. Then, they register for an account, log in, and observe the preferences and resume file are present under their new profile.
prerequisites: Session/cookie persistence enabled, document storage functional, anonymous onboarding enabled, registration possible.
stepsToPerform: 1. Start on the homepage as an anonymous visitor. 2. Complete the onboarding questions and upload a resume. 3. Submit and view personalized results. 4. Navigate away from results and back to onboarding section in the same session. 5. Confirm all preferences and upload still visible/active. 6. Initiate action triggering registration (e.g., apply or save job). 7. Complete new account registration and login. 8. Go to profile preferences and resume upload section. 9. Confirm all previously input preferences and resume are present. 10. Optionally, try new search and confirm preferences are reflected.
expectedResult: All preferences and uploaded documents are retained across anonymous browsing and are linked to the account after signup, per user state.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Hold preferences and uploaded documents against the seeker for the duration of an anonymous visit, and against the account thereafter.

title: Verify seeker can remove their resume and clear their preferences with all data deleted
description: Confirms that when a seeker requests, their uploaded resume and all captured preferences are fully deleted from both session and account scope, and no remnant or PII is retained. Protects privacy and compliance. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: An authenticated seeker (after registration and onboarding) accesses their data/preferences dashboard and uses the provided UI to remove resume and clear all preference selections. The system must immediately remove these items, update the UI to reflect empty profile/preference state, and leave no way to retrieve or restore data from within the product.
prerequisites: Active user account with at least one uploaded resume and completed preferences, data deletion/removal feature enabled.
stepsToPerform: 1. Log in as registered user with test data (e.g., 'test+removal@example.com'). 2. Go to preferences and resume management section. 3. Confirm preferences and an uploaded resume file are present. 4. Click to 'Remove Resume.' 5. Confirm upload is deleted and UI no longer shows attachment. 6. Click to 'Clear All Preferences.' 7. Confirm all preference fields are blanked and no filter values persist. 8. Attempt to trigger search/job match; confirm results are now generic. 9. Log out and log back in; verify data is still deleted. 10. Optionally, check settings or profile for absence of any residual data or undo/recovery option.
expectedResult: Resume and all preferences are fully deleted and do not appear anywhere in UI, search, or data store for the seeker.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Allow the seeker to remove their resume and clear their preferences.

title: Verify all personal details and uploaded documents are handled according to data protection obligations
description: This test validates that all personal information and uploaded resumes are collected, stored, and deleted strictly according to data protection requirements throughout the entire seeker onboarding journey. This protects users from PII leakage, ensures data minimization, and enforces user-driven data removal requests. Automation: HIGH — log and database assertions for PII/document lifecycle.
testDescription: A new seeker provides personal details and uploads a resume during onboarding without registration. The user then deletes both the uploaded resume and their preferences, both prior to and after registering for an account. The test checks that all personal data and documents are stored only for the permitted session/account scope, are not accessible after explicit deletion, and are never exposed in logs, caches, or unauthorized endpoints. Audit records must exist for storage and erasure events, with masking where required.
prerequisites: Platform is deployed with compliance mode enabled and audit logging active. Data protection officer permissions for log access. No seeker account or anonymous session exists.
stepsToPerform: 1. Navigate to the platform's home page as a new anonymous user. 2. Complete onboarding questionnaire with personal details: use test+pii@example.com, working arrangement 'Hybrid', salary '85000', location 'Canada', and other required fields. 3. Upload a resume file named 'resume-pii-test.pdf' containing fictitious PII (e.g., 'Test PII Name, test+pii@example.com'). 4. Confirm personalized job listings are shown and resume is visible in seeker session/profile. 5. Request deletion of the uploaded resume and verify UI and API indicate success. 6. Request clearing of all provided preferences via the designated UI control. 7. Inspect audit logs and backend storage: confirm PII fields and document no longer exist for the anonymous session. 8. Register for an account using 'test+pii2@example.com' and confirm new profile does not retain deleted resume/preference data. 9. Re-upload resume and set new preferences post-registration. 10. Request deletion again after registration; confirm deletion is reflected in storage and audit trail. 11. Query backend logs, cache, and response payloads for both deleted and masked PII/resume data. 12. Attempt API and UI access to deleted data; confirm all return 'not found' or equivalent status.
expectedResult: There is no residual personal data (PII or documents) present after deletion, both in the session scope and after account creation. Audit logs record all data storage and deletion events, with masking of sensitive fields. Data is never exposed in raw form via logs, responses, or unauthorized endpoints at any time.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Handle uploaded documents and personal details in line with applicable data protection obligations.

title: Verify E2E flow: complete onboarding, upload resume, view results, edit preferences, act on listing, register, and confirm data carryover
description: This test ensures the full lifecycle of seeker onboarding from anonymous journey through registration: capturing and using preferences and uploaded documents, carrying data across sessions, editing preferences, and maintaining a frictionless pre-registration experience. Automation: HIGH — covers UI, backend and data persistence.
testDescription: A new seeker visits the platform and completes the onboarding questionnaire, specifying all preferences and uploading a valid resume. The seeker reviews personalized results, edits select preferences to broaden listings, then applies for a job which triggers registration. After registering, the user verifies all previously submitted preferences and the resume are present in the account profile, with job matches updated and appropriately filtered.
prerequisites: No seeker account or session exists. Personal test data and a synthetic resume file ('test-resume-onboard.pdf'), platform is online.
stepsToPerform: 1. Access the home page as a new (anonymous) seeker. 2. Fill in all onboarding questionnaire fields: working arrangement 'Remote', motivation 'Career progression', salary '90000', location 'USA', job titles 'Product Manager', category 'IT', experience '7', education 'Bachelor', benefit 'Flexible schedule'. 3. Upload a PDF resume file named 'test-resume-onboard.pdf' (<5MB) in a supported format. 4. Submit the questionnaire and confirm display of personalized job results matching entered preferences. 5. Edit two preferences: change salary to '100000', add 'Hybrid' to working arrangement; submit changes. 6. Observe results update, with constraint indicators if listings reduce. 7. Select a job listing and click 'Apply', triggering registration flow prompt. 8. Register with 'test+e2e01@example.com' and set a password. 9. Upon redirect to account dashboard/home, verify uploaded resume and all onboarding preferences are displayed in the new profile. 10. Perform a search and validate job matches reflect all provided preferences. 11. Edit a preference post-registration and confirm job results adjust accordingly. 12. Log out and back in, confirming all data persists.
expectedResult: All onboarding inputs (preferences and resume) are visible in the user's account after registration, preferences and resume are used in job matching before and after sign-up, edits to preferences correctly update results, and no onboarding input is lost across the anonymous-to-registered transition.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Preferences captured before registration carry over into the account when the seeker signs up.

title: Verify E2E flow: skip fields, partial questionnaire, upload resume (all valid/invalid states), remove data, start registration, and confirm data deletion
description: This test explores all possible onboarding actions where the seeker skips fields, enters both valid and invalid resume uploads, removes data, and validates correct handling of incomplete or deleted information on transition to registration. The test protects against orphaned or incorrectly retained data and ensures all error and deletion paths function. Automation: HIGH — covers UI error display, backend validation, and cleanup.
testDescription: A new seeker initiates the onboarding questionnaire but only answers a subset of fields, skipping non-required questions. The user uploads a resume (tests both valid and invalid scenarios: unsupported format, oversize file) and removes it afterward. The test verifies that preferences and documents are correctly marked as provided or unanswered, that invalid resume uploads are rejected with clear reasons, and that after requesting data deletion and beginning the registration process, no deleted preferences or resume reappear in the new account profile.
prerequisites: Platform accepts all file types and error responses as defined in requirements. No account or previous session. Synthetic test files: 'resume-valid.pdf', 'resume-oversize.pdf' (e.g., 10MB), 'resume-unsupported.txt'.
stepsToPerform: 1. Go to platform home as anonymous. 2. Begin onboarding, answer only 'location' as 'UK' and 'job titles' as 'Developer'; skip all other fields. 3. Attempt resume upload with 'resume-unsupported.txt' (invalid format); observe error stating format unsupported. 4. Upload 'resume-oversize.pdf' (10MB); observe error indicating file size limit exceeded. 5. Upload 'resume-valid.pdf' (supported, under size limit); confirm resume appears in session/profile. 6. Remove uploaded resume and verify UI/API show it as deleted. 7. Use UI control to clear all entered preferences. 8. Inspect job results: confirm match reflects only provided fields, unfilled fields are marked 'not answered', and no resume is used in matching. 9. Begin registration after acting on a listing (e.g., apply/save). 10. Register with 'test+partialdelete@example.com'. 11. After account creation, confirm no cleared preferences or deleted resumes are present in the new profile. 12. Attempt to access deleted resume/preferences via API/DB; verify access is blocked or data is absent.
expectedResult: Only submitted questionnaire fields are recorded; skipped fields are shown as unanswered. Invalid resume uploads are rejected with precise user-facing errors. Removed data (resume, cleared preferences) is not visible or accessible post-deletion, and is not imported into the new account after registration.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Record which preferences were provided and which were left unanswered... Allow the seeker to remove their resume and clear their preferences.
